chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Forming his first band at the Madhouse
summary: Back at the Madhouse he leads a five-piece group of guitar, banjo, bass, drums and piano with Harold Waters and Harry Morris.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So, when you came back from the war, you went back into the Madhouse. Had it changed in the year and a half or so, or was it the same?
No, no. I think it run on the same. They don't change things. They still knock people in their heads and
And sang, and drink their liquor and have a good time and everybody thought it was going to go on forever.
But this time, you got a band together.

Not a real large band, let's see, I had a guitar, I had a tenor banjo -- no, a banjereen, the short necked banjo. See, it wasn't a long one, but I had a guitar, a bass, and I had a drum. And the piano. Those five people were there.
Do you remember any of the musicians who were with you?

Oh, yes. I remember Harold Waters, and then there was, what was his name, the very good drummer -- in fact this drummer came along with me. Harry Morris. Harry Morris was one of the greatest drummers. I don't know, he loved Philadelphia so much he never got to New York. But, there was nothing in New York, Chick Webb or nobody else, that was any better than he in those days, you see what I mean.
He was very good, but he loved Philadelphia and he started raising a family there and then he never got out.
